subject: astronomy
title: Solar & Lunar Eclipses: Types
welcome_lead: Eclipses come in a few flavours — total, partial and annular.
meta_desc: KS3 astronomy: types of eclipses, watching safely.
final_note: Never look at the Sun without special filters — eclipse or not.

concepts.def: Sun or Moon is fully blocked.

walkthroughs.body_html: In a total solar eclipse, the Moon perfectly covers the Sun for a few minutes. The corona glows around the dark Moon.
When the Moon is a little far from Earth, it can't cover the whole Sun. A bright ring remains — an annular eclipse.
Never stare at the Sun with naked eyes. Use special solar eclipse glasses. Lunar eclipses are safe to watch directly.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a solar eclipse and a lunar eclipse?
options: Solar eclipses happen by day, lunar at night - that is the only difference.
In a solar eclipse the Moon blocks the Sun; in a lunar eclipse Earth's shadow covers the Moon.
Because they are the brightest objects in the universe.
Lunar eclipses are more dangerous.

options: It moves backwards.
Lunar eclipses are more dangerous.
It is too small to be a planet.
It does not clear its orbital neighbourhood of similar-sized bodies.
